clue.text: Drink made from stimulating leaves, with nothing put in

indicators.note: put in tells us the zero goes inside the word for the leaves

parts.note: coca is the South American shrub whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hot drink brewed from stimulating leaves, with nothing added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places O (nothing) inside COCA, between its third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Touch earth unexpectedly, and get a shock

definitions.text: Touch earth unexpectedly, and get a shock

parts.words: Touch earth unexpectedly, and get a shock
parts.note: reads like an electrical accident when a wire touches earth, but describes an aircraft coming down violently

explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' and 'shock' suggest electricity; the real picture is an emergency landing that jolts everyone aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that comes down by force in an emergency meets the ground abruptly and roughly.

clue.text: Pet suppressing whimper in house at war

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the cat word contains the whimper word

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
to pule is to whimper or whine

explanation.surface: A pet stifling its whining in a household full of quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capulets are Juliet's family, at feud with the Montagues in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Capulets are a noble family locked in a feud with the Montagues.

clue.text: A plane taken to old friend

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A plane flown to visit a longtime friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for pal, used informally in English.

clue.text: Rejected reproduction in their edition as fraud

indicators.note: in tells us the turned-round copy sits inside the rearranged letters
a new edition of a text is a reworked version, so the letters of their are rearranged
rejected means sent back, so the word for reproduction is read backwards

parts.note: a reproduction is a copy

explanation.surface: A rejected reprint of their edition exposed as a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edition' is an unusual anagram signal: a new edition reworks a text. 'Rejected' reverses the copy word, and 'in' puts it after the first letter of the rearranged THEIR (HRITE).
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocrite is a sham who pretends to virtues they lack, a kind of impostor.

clue.text: German's angst, missing a number of scores

parts.note: Hun is a dated, derogatory name for a German

indicators.note: missing tells us the letter A is taken out of the word for angst

parts.note: angst is dread

explanation.surface: A German's anxiety at missing several goals.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, and five scores make the number. 'missing' takes the A from DREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Five times twenty, so a count expressible as several twenties.

clue.text: Army push to get off the ground in exercise

parts.note: a press is a forceful push or drive, as of an army advancing
up means raised off the ground

explanation.surface: A military offensive struggling to get going during manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' also hints that it is a staple of military drill, lifting the body by the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym movement raising the body from the floor using the arms, the US push-up.

clue.text: Set of wooden steps

parts.note: looks like a staircase or ladder, but describes a sequence of dance steps done in wooden shoes

explanation.walkthrough: 'steps' are dance moves and 'wooden' refers to the footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk dance performed in wooden-soled shoes that tap out rhythms.

clue.text: Royal personage put in cooler by army

parts.note: in is taken as written
a fan is something that cools
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A royal figure locked up in a cell by the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' suggests prison slang, but means a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king.

clue.text: Pint with no head — that is weird

indicators.note: with no head tells us to drop the first letter of the drink word

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer

explanation.surface: A flat pint of beer with no froth on top is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests the froth on a beer, but it means the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Piece of equipment I can change inside cooker, say

indicators.note: inside tells us the shuffled letters go within the word for the cooker

parts.note: a cooker is a cooking apple, so an apple is an example of one

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of I can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kitchen gadget I can swap inside the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooker' looks like the oven but is a cooking apple, the 'say' marking an example. 'change' rearranges I CAN to IANC.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine for a household task.

clue.text: Some say leader of Mercia once was tender

indicators.note: some say signals that the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, the Anglo-Saxon kingdom in central England

explanation.surface: Some claim a former ruler of Mercia was a gentle soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like an adjective (gentle) but is the verb or noun meaning a proposal. Offa built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to put forward or present something, as with a bid or proposal.

clue.text: Where one may sleep with lots of fellow-undergraduates

definitions.text: Where one may sleep with lots of fellow-undergraduates

parts.words: Where one may sleep with lots of fellow-undergraduates
parts.note: sounds risqué, but it describes the university building where many students lodge

explanation.walkthrough: The suggestive reading is the misdirection; the place is simply student accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A university building housing many students, where each has a bed.

clue.text: Having a temperature and lacking energy, but got up

parts.note: lacking energy means tired

explanation.surface: Feverish and exhausted, yet still managed to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' looks like rose from bed, but means dressed, as in 'got up in fancy dress'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got up in something is to be dressed in it, clothed.

clue.text: It expresses one's disapproval for the cane

definitions.meaning: the rude blowing noise made with the tongue between the lips
the fruit that grows on a cane, a woody stem

explanation.walkthrough: 'cane' suggests a punishment rod, fitting the disapproval, but it is the plant stem the fruit grows on.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit grows on canes, and blowing one is a derisive noise.

clue.text: One hung by the neck seen to breathe with difficulty, about to die

indicators.note: about tells us the panting word goes round the word for dying

parts.note: to pant is to breathe with difficulty
to die is to end

explanation.surface: A hanged man seen gasping for air, about to die.
explanation.walkthrough: The gallows picture misleads: the thing hung round the neck is a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is an ornament worn on a chain around the neck.

clue.text: Specifies article to be supported in America

indicators.note: in a down clue, to be supported means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the is the definite article
to specify is to state

explanation.surface: Stipulates that an item must be backed in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to be supported' means the article sits on top, held up by the verb below it.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is an informal name for the United States.

clue.text: Endlessly avoid little boy? He preferred little girls

indicators.note: endlessly tells us to remove the final letter of the word for avoid

parts.note: to avoid is to dodge
a son is someone's little boy

explanation.surface: Constantly steering clear of the little lad, he favoured young girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Dodgson was Lewis Carroll, author of Alice in Wonderland, known for befriending young girls such as Alice Liddell. 'Endlessly' takes the last E off DODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgson, writing as Lewis Carroll, enjoyed the company of children like Alice Liddell rather than boys.

clue.text: Traditionally feminine work that helps one to unwind

definitions.meaning: the female side of a family is called the ... side

definitions.text: work that helps one to unwind
definitions.meaning: a stick holding wool or flax as it is drawn off for spinning

explanation.walkthrough: 'unwind' looks like relaxation, but means the fibre being drawn off the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning stick was women's work, hence its sense of the female line.

clue.text: Brief communication raising school rent

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the school word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A short letter about a school putting up its fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns ETON into NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for a short message.

clue.text: Betray nerves, having sunk millions into multiple bet

indicators.note: having sunk into means the letter for millions is placed within the word for the bet

parts.note: a treble is a bet on three races, with winnings rolled from one to the next
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Feeling nervous after sinking millions into an accumulator bet.
explanation.walkthrough: A treble is a British betting term for a three-leg accumulator.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake or quiver is how a nervous person gives themselves away.

clue.text: Tourist finally overcoming currency difficulty

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting on top of the next piece
finally points to the last letter of the word tourist

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A traveller eventually getting past money problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' puts T above ROUBLE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble means a problem or difficulty.

clue.text: Notice ruffian goes round boasting

indicators.note: goes round means the ruffian word encircles the notice word

parts.note: a bravo is a hired thug or assassin
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Note how the thug swaggers about, boasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravo' here is the old word for a hired villain, not the cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness or swagger, close to bragging.

clue.text: What's available from letters of flats? Something not to be overlooked

definitions.text: What's available from letters of flats?
definitions.meaning: the letters of flats can be rearranged to spell the word for final, but there is no E in them for the word meaning smallest
the stock phrase for an item mentioned at the end that is still important

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic riddle: FLATS rearranges to LAST, but contains no E, so it cannot make LEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a final item that still deserves full attention.

clue.text: Number of stopping train

definitions.meaning: read as numb-er, something that numbs: an anaesthetic for one area
a train calling at every station

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but 'one that numbs', a local anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs, and a local train stops everywhere.

clue.text: Not being disturbed by Matilda's behaviour

definitions.meaning: resting undisturbed, as something left where it was
Matilda, in Hilaire Belloc's Cautionary Tales, told dreadful fibs and was burned to death

explanation.walkthrough: Belloc's poem is 'Matilda, Who told Lies, and was Burned to Death'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things left where they lie are undisturbed, and Matilda's habit was telling untruths.

clue.text: I burn out in academic post

indicators.note: in tells us the letter I goes inside the word for burn out

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch out

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted by burnout in a university job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn out' reads as exhaustion in the surface, but it means scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called a chair, the senior academic position.

clue.text: Oil spilled in Baltic run

indicators.note: spilled suggests letters scattered about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Oil spilt during a shipping voyage on the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' rearranges BALTIC RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is a slippery substance used to reduce friction, an example of the type.

clue.text: Revolutionary general left a lot still imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned tells us the word for still is held inside the word for lot

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
still, meaning up to now, is yet

explanation.surface: The revolutionary general left a great many people still behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'many', but A is taken alone and 'lot' means fate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Lafayette was a French general in both the American and French revolutions.

clue.text: Explanation of grand failure

parts.note: G is short for grand, slang for a thousand
a failure is a loss

explanation.surface: An account of why a grand undertaking failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloss is a note explaining a word or passage in a text.
